newsitem.title: FRANCE: Printers' strike halts France's main dailies.
newsitem.headline: Printers' strike halts France's main dailies.

text.p: France's main newspapers failed to appear on Thursday because of a 24-hour strike by a printers' union protesting cuts in state subsidies and pushing for a lower retirement age.

Newspapers like Le Monde, Le Figaro and Liberation were absent from newsstands while a few regional titles appeared as normal. Some dailies were available on the Internet computer network even if they did not make it on to paper.
"The extent of this first halt of all forms of press shows the urgency of opening true negotiations," the printers' branch of the Communist-led CGT union said in a statement.

The union is protesting at reductions in state subsidies to the media, suppression of tax breaks and rising postal charges. Urging meetings with bosses and unions, it said it would publish detailed demands in coming weeks.
It also wants to highlight its demands for retirement at 55 instead of at 60, a measure the CGT says will help cut unemployment of a record 12.8 percent of the workforce.
